fig1_unruh_planck.svg: A uniformly accelerated observer sees the inertial vacuum as a thermal bath. The Rindler-mode occupation $|\beta_\omega|^2$ built only from the Bogoliubov ratio $e^{-2\pi c\omega/a}$ (unruh_occupation, open circles) lands exactly on the Planck/Bose-Einstein law $1/(e^{\hbar\omega/k_BT_U}-1)$ (bose_occupation, solid) at the Unruh temperature $T_U=\hbar a/2\pi c k_B$ — the Fermi law (dashed) shown for contrast. Mode mixing $\Rightarrow$ a genuinely thermal spectrum.
fig2_hawking_temperature.svg: Hawking temperature versus mass from hawking_temperature(): $T_H=\hbar c^3/8\pi GMk_B$ falls as $1/M$ (a straight line of slope $-1$ on log-log axes). A solar-mass hole sits at $\sim6\times10^{-8}$ K, far below the $2.725$ K CMB (dashed) so it absorbs more than it radiates, while a $1$ kg hole would glow at $\sim10^{23}$ K. With the horizon ($r_s=2GM/c^2$) shrinking too, the hole radiates ever faster as it evaporates.
